records.mutation: diagnose the self-refutation loop: an all-branches-impossible proof means a false added assumption, and a person's options are the union across live branches, not one branch at a time
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8; 2 truncated and all eight burned 13k-16.4k tokens. Every rollout split into the two readings, proved inside each that a speaker's own value pins the partner, declared both readings impossible, and then reported a value it had just refuted -- five reported a factor whose refutation they restated in the same breath, one reported a value it explicitly called wrong. One rollout actually reached the balanced equal-split candidate, argued it away as impossible, and reported a neighbour instead. The incumbent asks the student to intersect constraints across readings, but the student never gets there because it treats the collapse as settled truth. So I made the self-refutation itself the trigger: an all-branches-impossible proof means a false assumption was added, and options are the union across live branches, plus a rule not to argue away a candidate that passed.

records.mutation: prepend an up-front target-and-form specification (which quantity, reduced exact form) replacing the round-11 undetermined-coefficients clause, keeping the setup and a compressed commit/no-restart rule
records.subagent_summary: All eight fresh rollouts were correct, so train is saturated and only length and transfer carry information. Six finished in 5.8k-8.2k tokens, but the outlier ran to 14.6k because after reaching the locus it parametrized by an angle and fought to eliminate the cosine, deriving two contradictory expressions for it and spending thousands of tokens reconciling them. Rounds 5-11 all attacked that self-audit loop with meta-discipline or alternative machinery and every one lost transfer, so the loop is not the lever. Instead I add the cheapest reusable guard that costs no derivation work: pin the requested quantity and its required form up front, since a sound derivation reported as the neighbouring object or left unreduced scores zero, and that risk exists on every problem rather than just this one.

records.mutation: replace bare bound-plus-witness with symmetry-invariance-or-bound stop licence, cap re-checks at two agreeing passes, and forbid headings/re-derivation in the write-up
records.subagent_summary: Two of eight scored. No failure was mathematical: all eight reached the value inside the first 3-7k of ~52-62k characters. Four never closed reasoning at all, still numerically re-testing rotations (98-182 rotation mentions, 45-83 restarts). The two decisive failures did close reasoning and began a multi-heading write-up, but spent their whole visible budget restating the givens and re-deriving the overlap, and were truncated one step short of combining the numbers; both successes reached that combining step with a shorter reply. So the incumbent transcribe-the-numbers clause fires too weakly. This revision replaces the abstract bound-plus-witness stop with a two-way licence to halt (a symmetry showing the parameter never mattered, or a bound plus an attaining case), caps re-checking explicitly, and forbids headings and re-derivation in the write-up.

records.mutation: add a residual-degree audit (subtracting a line leaves the leading term, so degree stays d, never d-1) and attach the dropped-factor check to the m*d line
records.subagent_summary: 4 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct with ZERO token-limit truncations, so the position-indexed residual framing fixed last round only losses. Every remaining failure is now degree bookkeeping or a retreat to a single factor: three finishers subtracted a constant term of the target instead of the whole affine target, declared the residual degree d-1, and reported a budget one factor short per piece; one dropped reusability entirely and answered the bare piece count; one applied the d-root cap to the whole pattern and answered the bare degree. The revision therefore adds an explicit residual-degree audit stating that subtracting a line leaves the leading term alone so the residual keeps full degree d and never d-1, and folds the dropped-factor check directly onto the m*d line where the collapse happens.

records.mutation: validate each algebraic rewrite by one-number evaluation before solving; treat no real root as a rewrite error and recompute dependent quantities from the relation
records.subagent_summary: Only 3 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct, a sharp drop, and every failure came from the same place: the sign/factor bookkeeping in one algebraic rewrite. Three variants of the reduced quadratic appeared across rollouts and only one was right; wrong ones gave a complex or spurious root, after which three rollouts burned the whole budget rationalizing, one shipped an invented value, and one kept a bad root and mis-derived the dependent coordinate. The incumbent says to discard bad roots but never tells the student to validate the rewrite that produced them, so I added a cheap one-number check of each cross-multiplication or absorbed constant, reframed no-real-root as evidence against the rewrite rather than the problem, and required dependent quantities to be recomputed from the defining relation instead of copied.

records.mutation: replace abstract atom-counting with a concrete enumerate-and-tabulate rule once the run count is small, and require every part to be read off that single table
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 1/8. The incumbent already fixes the first part: five rollouts derived 1/2^(free) correctly there. Every failure came on the later part, where the run immediately abandoned the free-step sample space and asserted "each item is equally likely in any position", reporting 1/n; two others burned the whole token budget oscillating between 1/n and a power of two without ever writing out cases. So the abstract atom vocabulary is understood but not acted on. The revision makes the space concrete: size it, and once it is small, tabulate one row per run with the resulting configuration spelled out, then count rows for every part. It keeps the LIFO orientation fact (a pile bottom is its earliest arrival), bans dividing by n, and legitimizes two parts sharing a value so the student stops switching methods to force them apart.

records.mutation: enforce strict ordering: finish small instances numerically before opening any symbolic route, plus an explicit cost tripwire on long-product coefficient extraction
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling scored 0 of 8 and all eight ran to the token cap without stating any result. Seven abandoned the small-instance route almost immediately (several started it, then dropped it mid-setup) in favour of a symbolic recast, and then sank the entire budget on one shared sink: extracting a low-order coefficient of a very long product via elementary symmetric or harmonic sums, looping on sign and index conventions. One reached the right shape but declared it contradictory after botching its own small-case check, and one drifted into an ever-messier expression and gave up. Past successes all came from finishing a few tiny instances numerically first, so the revision makes that ordering strict rather than merely recommended and adds an explicit cost tripwire that names the long-product coefficient hunt as the route to abandon.

records.mutation: keep verbatim opening and small-cases clause; replace the never-used exact-fractions clause with a uniqueness-forcing-condition rule for underdetermined-looking givens
records.subagent_summary: Round 12 sampling returned 8/8 with clean stops at 3.0-7.0k tokens, so train has been pinned at 1.0 for twelve rounds and only transfer can move J. Trace evidence: the incumbent's exact-fractions clause is never exercised (zero hits in all eight traces), so that slot is dead weight, while the students spend their length on underdetermination anxiety (7-21 uses of 'intended', 13-29 hedges per trace) circling which value the setup means before any arithmetic. Prior rounds proved the opening must stay verbatim and that scope-labeling, gcd-naming, anti-rumination, representation-switching and output-form tails all lost ground. So I reclaim only the dead clause with the untested lever the traces actually need: when the givens look too weak, do not argue the reading, locate the uniqueness-forcing condition (integrality, extremum, symmetry, non-degeneracy) and let it settle the choice.

records.mutation: add an anti-speculation rule (test the first plausible structure against the data at once, never detour through inverses) targeting the observed hypothesis-survey stall, and generalize the sum/difference step as a symmetric-data lever
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct, all finishing in 4.1k-6.5k tokens by committing to the shared-center antisymmetric pair and solving the two supplied values by sum and difference. The lone failure never reached that structure at all: it opened by naming eight unknown coefficients, then spent the entire 16384-token budget cycling through speculative hypotheses (are they inverses, reciprocals, scalar multiples, one plus a constant), repeatedly noting each was unpromising without ever testing one against the data, and drifted into degree-8 coefficient extraction of the composition. Prior revisions ordered recentering first but never forbade this open-ended hypothesis survey. The revision therefore adds an explicit anti-speculation rule (commit to the first plausible structure and check it against the given numbers at once) and names the inverse detour as the observed trap, while preserving the proven centered core.

records.mutation: ban the permutation/cycle-type translation outright and make row-by-row iteration the only sanctioned method; name reading one pass as position pairs (hence period 2) as the specific trap, and add an anti-loop exit
records.subagent_summary: Only 1 of 8 scored and 5 hit the 16384-token cap. Every failure did the same thing: it correctly rewrote the row for the smallest sizes, then translated that single pass into a table of position pairs, called the composite a product of disjoint transpositions, and concluded period 2 or an exponent one too small. Three then spent thousands of tokens in visible loops ('this is confusing', 'is it a 3-cycle? no, a 2-cycle?') trying to reconcile self-contradictory index maps against their own rows. The incumbent tells the student to trace concretely and warns swap-shaped stages need not have period 2, yet the student still abandons the row for cycle vocabulary the moment one pass finishes. The revision therefore forbids the permutation translation entirely, makes repeated passes the only evidence of a return, and gives an explicit exit when repetition starts.
